chunks: From him, from Safwan and Fadala, from al-Ala' ibn Muhammad, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man manumitted his slave conditionally (mudabbarr), then he [the master] needed the money. He said: When he needs the money, it is for him to sell [the slave] if he wishes. And if he frees him, that [the value] is from the third.

key_terms.دَبَّرَ: To manumit a slave conditionally (making them free upon a specific event, typically the master's death)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a master who needs money while his slave is conditionally manumitted (mudabbarr)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the status of the *mudabbarr* (a slave manumitted upon a specified condition, such as death or payment) when the master requires liquidity before the condition is met. It establishes that the master retains the right to sell the slave, but if he chooses to emancipate him prematurely, the slave's value is deducted from the master's estate as part of the *third* (one-third) reserved for bequests, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the transition of ownership and debt settlement.
